surface: One frame on the great ofrenda stands empty.
truth: La Golondrina's portrait hung on the great ofrenda. Someone took it tonight, before the first song.
share_text: La Golondrina's portrait is gone from the ofrenda — someone took it tonight.

surface: Bruno was seen with a sack near the ofrenda at dusk.
truth: A lie Ramón spread — the sack held marigold flowers for grave 12. Carmen watched him fill it.
share_text: They say Bruno carried a sack past the ofrenda at dusk — right when the portrait vanished.

surface: Carmen keeps pictures for her nameless graves, they say.
truth: Another lie Ramón spread — the widow tends the forgotten out of kindness, not theft.
share_text: They whisper Carmen collects pictures — for those graves of hers with no names.

surface: Something glints beneath the empty frame.
truth: A mother-of-pearl guitar pick lies under the bare frame — the kind a troubadour plays with, dropped in a hurry.
share_text: A guitar pick was found under the empty frame — the kind a troubadour plays.

surface: A child heard humming by the great ofrenda.
truth: Violeta heard someone humming La Golondrina's own tune by the frames at dusk — a troubadour's habit, not a gravedigger's.
share_text: Someone was heard humming La Golondrina's tune beside the ofrenda that night.

surface: Only the thief could know the frame's flaw.
truth: The stolen frame had a crack down the left side — Ramón described it to himself without ever being told.
share_text: Ramón knew the frame's crack ran down the left — a detail only the thief could know.

surface: A silver glint in a troubadour's hand.
truth: Tía Luz saw Ramón pocket something silver-bright near the cantina — she told only Sefa, in confidence.
share_text: Ramón was seen pocketing something silver near the cantina that night.

surface: Fresh wax on a troubadour's cuff.
truth: The ofrenda candle nearest the bare frame was re-lit by a thief's hand — fresh wax still clings to Ramón's sleeve.
share_text: Fresh candle wax clings to Ramón's sleeve — and the ofrenda candle by the empty frame burned new.

surface: Bruno's sack held flowers, not a frame.
truth: Carmen watched Bruno fill his sack with marigolds for grave 12 — flowers, nothing more.
share_text: Bruno's sack held marigolds for grave 12 — Carmen watched him fill it.

surface: Carmen tended candles all through dusk.
truth: Aurelio saw Carmen at Solorio's grave through dusk — new flames kept appearing, she never left.
share_text: Carmen was lighting candles at Solorio's grave all through dusk — Aurelio saw the flames.

surface: Ramón hums La Golondrina's tunes like they're his own.
truth: Her candle burned brighter every year while his name dimmed — he could not bear to watch her remembered.
share_text: Ramón could not bear it — her candle burning brighter every year while his own name dimmed.

surface: Grave 37 has no photo, no name — fresh marigolds anyway.
truth: It is Solorio's grave. He fades because nobody remembers his name — say his name and he comes back. He saw the thief at the frames.
share_text: Grave 37 is Solorio's. Say his name and he remembers himself — he saw the thief at the frames.
